subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Documentaries, Wines, Mind-Boggling “Acquired Savants,” Games, and Defining “Spirituality”

bullets.title: Domaine Tempier’s Bandol Rosé
bullets.note: Despite all the anti-alcohol zeitgeist, I still enjoy sipping a glass of wine while cooking on the weekend. This rosé is bone-dry, savory, and nothing like sweet, grocery-store pink wine. Domaine Tempier is a family estate in Bandol on France’s Provence coast. In the early twentieth century, Lucien Peyraud and his wife Lulu built the domaine’s reputation by betting on [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), a harder to grow grape. Fun fact for the foodies: Lulu [became a mentor](https://priorworld.com/editorial/alice-waters-lulu-peyraud-prior-wine) to legendary chef [Alice Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Waters) of Chez Panisse fame.

bullets.title: Crip Camp: A Disability Revolution
bullets.note: This film was just what I needed after a rough day. Short description: “A groundbreaking summer camp galvanizes a group of teens with disabilities to help build a movement, forging a new path toward greater equality.” It has [100% on Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/crip_camp) and [won the Sundance Film Festival’s Audience Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crip_Camp#Awards_and_nominations) in 2020. You can [find the trailer here](youtube.com/watch?feature=youtu.be&si=A7J785Vw2eRvc93y&v=XRrIs22plz0).

bullets.title: Coyote is the card game
bullets.note:
that I co-created with Exploding Kittens. It won the _Pop Insider_ “Best Geeky Game” of 2025 and also “Best Stocking Filler” in the MadeForMums Toy Awards 2025 (UK). The game is available at [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Exploding-Kittens-Ferriss-Present-Minutes/dp/B0FBT88VRJ/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20), [Target](https://www.target.com/p/exploding-kittens-coyote-card-game/-/A-94284795#lnk=sametab), [Walmart](https://www.walmart.com/ip/Coyote-Scramble/14312603259), [Exploding Kittens](https://www.explodingkittens.com/products/coyote), and more, but I wanted to make it available for free to those who can’t afford it, or who can’t buy it in their countries.  
​  
Here’s how to print out the deck:  
​  
​**1.** [Click here to download](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eF-uwVnPwansbj9PucwZA7df7XlyTgbS/view?usp=sharing) the print-to-play PDF file and [click here to download](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k5sRzW3__DvHfGBtonfCajRr4pT4AxNk/view?usp=sharing) the instructions.

**2.** You will need a total of 67 standard-sized playing cards (2.5" x 3.5"). [Here is one option for getting it done](https://www.amazon.com/Apostrophe-Games-Blank-Playing-Finish/dp/B01H4CZQ14/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20), unless you already have enough cards at home that you are no longer playing with. You can also print on regular or stock paper and cut out the cards.

**3.** Purchase [this Avery label template](https://www.avery.com/products/name-badges/25395) (#25395, 2-1/3" x 3-3/8", 80 name badges, 8 per sheet).

**4.** Put the Avery templates in your printer.

**5.** Print [the cards PDF file](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eF-uwVnPwansbj9PucwZA7df7XlyTgbS/view?usp=sharing). We suggest doing a test run with one page.

**6.** Once printed, put each label on each playing card.

**7\.** Print [the instructions PDF](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k5sRzW3__DvHfGBtonfCajRr4pT4AxNk/view?usp=sharing).  
​  
Enjoy!
